There's many interesting topics to consider, although you probably will have to consider which audience you want to appeal to. A few things that sprung to my mind:

  1. "Killer" Games - Do video games really turn people violent? (TL/DR: They don't, or at least there's no serious academic support for claims as made by Thompson or, in a more recent example, Germany's Interior Minister Thomas de Maiziere. It may be pointed out that games can also have a cathartic effect - i.e. they allow people to vent rather than to take out their anger on other people, although it may also be argued that games may feed into the delusions of potentially dangerous people - the prerequisite being that said people were delusional in the first place).

  2. The Rise and Fall of Indie Games - From humble beginnings to market breakthroughs like Minecraft, to the current over-saturation of the market coupled with the appearance of Non-Games like "Gone Home".

  3. GamerGate - Corruption, Misogyny, Clusterfuck? (May be hard to find unbiased sources for this - most media is staunchly anti-GamerGate, while pro-GG groups tend to behave very defensively when asked about the alleged harassment performed by the group. Also, positive reports about GG may lead SJWs to target you and try to get you fired).

  4. Speedrunning (Basically a kind of competition in which players try to make it through a game as quickly as possible. Has its own events such as AGDQ, many of which gather money for charities).

  5. Pokemon Go and Virtual Reality in Gaming - Pros and Cons (The phenomenon sees many couch potatoes go outside and socialize, but don't forget the game also tracks your every step, and its producer's didn't put it on the market without hoping for a fat profit).
